name: answer_option
description: FR-BB22 (roadmap section 2.2) -- ports the answer_options AND answer_translations tables from c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\BilimBaga\backend\migrations\009_questions.up.sql. The same two-tables-into-one collapse as question.json, for the same reason: BilimBaga used a per-locale row table (answer_translations) because its Postgres schema had no other way to hold multilingual text, and REQ-301's :localized_text is exactly that mechanism at the platform layer, so answer_translations has no independent existence in this pack. question_id is :string, queried: true, required: true. sort_order is :integer, queried: true, required: true. is_correct is :boolean, queried: true, required: true (source default FALSE). likert_weight is :decimal with decimal_precision: 5, decimal_scale: 2, queried: false, required: false -- both numbers are ported directly from the source's DECIMAL(5,2), not chosen independently. likert_polarity is :enum with enum_values ["positive","negative"], queried: false, required: false, ported from the source CHECK. text is :localized_text (source answer_translations.text) with locales ["kk","ru","en"], search_strategy "plain", queried: true, required: true. Foreign keys: fk_answer_option_question_id (field "question_id", references_entity "question"). Indexes: idx_answer_option_question_id over question_id, mirroring the source's idx_answer_options_question_id. is_correct and field-level redaction: is_correct is the field a candidate must never see, and this is exactly what Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants (REQ-231) -- field-level redaction that already exists -- is meant to govern. This pack does not configure a field grant; it only ensures is_correct is a first-class promoted field on its own record, so that redaction is expressible at all, which it would not be if answer options were nested inside the question's blob as a JSON array. This is the reason answer_option is authored as a separate entity type rather than a JSON array on question. No id, created_at, updated_at or created_by field is declared: the record subsystem mints record identity and the event store carries the audit timeline, so declaring these here would duplicate platform-owned state inside tenant content.
